Outline: Purpose: The dominant captive presents an injured hand, and Caelen realizes other prisoners may expect him to repeat the relief he gave the girl.
Prose:
The prisoner held out the hand again, closer this time, and turned it palm upward.

Two fingers wouldn't straighten.

Caelen looked more carefully. The knuckles were swollen, the skin stretched shiny over them. One finger lay at an angle that made his own hand ache in sympathy. He couldn't tell how old the injury was.

The prisoner pointed at the girl's back, then at the damaged hand.

Oh.

Caelen glanced at the girl. She was watching him now, her eyes moving between his face and the offered palm. She didn't look reassured by his expression.

"I don't know how I did that," he said quietly.

The prisoner waited.

Of course. It wasn't an answer if nobody understood it.

Caelen raised both hands, palms open, and shook his head. The injured fingers curled a little farther, then stopped. A muscle tightened along the prisoner's jaw.

"Not refusing," Caelen added, hearing the useless urgency in his own voice. "I just don't know."

He pointed at the hand and made a small questioning gesture. The prisoner brought it closer. Up close, Caelen could see old splits across the knuckles, dirt worked deep into the creases, and a fresh scrape along the wrist. There was no reason to think touching it would do anything except hurt.

Behind the broad shoulders, two other captives had stopped pretending not to watch. One rubbed an elbow. Another leaned far enough forward that a neighbor caught his arm and pulled him back.

Caelen's stomach tightened.

Whatever they thought they'd seen, it had already become more than a moment between him and the girl.

He looked at the prisoner, touched his own eyes, then pointed to the damaged fingers. Look first. Please let that much be clear.

After a pause, the prisoner nodded.

Caelen moved slowly, giving the offered hand time to pull away. He supported it beneath the wrist without trying to force the fingers straight. The whole room seemed to be waiting for something he wasn't sure he could give.

Caelen turned, keeping one hand near the girl's shoulder so she wouldn't twist into the wall again.

The biggest prisoner in the cell stood a few paces behind him. No cane, no ledger. Just a broad body planted in the open space the others had been so careful to avoid.

The prisoner spoke again.

Caelen caught none of it. He looked down at his own hand, then at the girl's face. Her brief relief had disappeared. She pulled the back of her blouse down over the wounds and began answering before he could say anything.

Her words came quickly. She pointed at Caelen, touched her own back, and stopped.

The prisoner held out a hand.

Caelen glanced at it. An order to stand aside? An invitation? Scarface had offered almost the same gesture, and he still didn't know what that had meant.

"I don't understand you," he said.

The prisoner looked from his mouth to his eyes. Whatever answer came back was slower, each unfamiliar word given its own space. Caelen understood no more of it than before.

He shook his head.

A murmur started near the far wall. The prisoner turned toward it, and it died away. When the broad face turned back, Caelen found himself resisting the urge to apologize for something he couldn't name.

The girl moved half a step toward him. Her fingers caught his forearm, but this time she wasn't pulling him closer. A small pressure urged his hand down.

Caelen let it fall to his side.

The prisoner noticed. Eyes followed the movement, lingered on his palm, then returned to the girl. Another question. This time she answered with one short word and kept her head lowered.

Caelen wished he knew whether she had just defended him or warned the other prisoner about him. He couldn't ask her. All he could do was stand there and watch the two of them decide what his hand had meant.
